scope: Preregistered native microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T residual-stream sub-4-bit scalar-angular versus grouped-VQ test on the frozen 1016-token protocol with 4-bit cascaded radial codec.

interpretation.supported: The A4 shape-gain result survives with the 4-bit radial codec and materially outperforms the matched Hadamard dynamic-A4 baseline. The shifted-radius control on the best A2 VQ condition still shows strong token-radius specificity.
interpretation.not_supported: Neither A3 scalar nor A2 scalar/VQ residual compression beats the matched A4 baseline. The preregistered sub-4-bit claim therefore stops here. A1 must remain closed.
interpretation.novelty_update: At A2, grouped VQ is far better than the scalar angular grid, so any future claim must not center on the scalar grid. The surviving empirical contribution is an A4 native-BitNet residual shape-gain representation with a compact radial side channel and hostile radius controls.
